# Lisbon and Porto Destination Guide

## Lisbon
Lisbon in late October sits around 18C by day and 12C at night, with occasional short showers. The Alfama and Baixa districts are the most walkable base for a first visit, both close to tram lines and within twenty minutes of most sights on foot.

### Getting around
A 24-hour Viva Viagem transit pass covers metro, tram, and bus. Trams 28 and 12 are the most scenic but also the most crowded with tourists; consider walking the route instead if you want photos.

### Where to stay
Mid-range hotels in Baixa run EUR 90-140 a night for two in late October. Chiado is quieter and slightly pricier; Alfama is more atmospheric but has more stairs and cobblestones.

### Day trips
The Douro Valley wine region is roughly 90 minutes by car or a guided coach tour, with half-day and full-day options. Sintra is closer, about 40 minutes by train, but gets very busy on weekends.

## Porto
Porto is smaller and easier to cover on foot. The Ribeira riverfront and the port wine cellars across the river in Vila Nova de Gaia are the two anchors of a short visit.

### Getting there from Lisbon
High-speed trains run hourly and take about three hours; book a few days ahead for the best fares.

### Food notes
Francesinha is the local specialty sandwich, heavy and worth sharing. Seafood is reliably good near the river. Reservations are rarely needed outside peak dinner hours.

### Practical notes
Both cities are safe for typical tourist areas. Pickpocketing on crowded trams is the most common issue reported. Tap water is safe to drink in both cities.
